subject: fix: serialize RunRequirement datetime for PostgreSQL JSONB storage (#5694)
message:
fix: serialize RunRequirement datetime for PostgreSQL JSONB storage (#5694)

Fixes #5661
Fixes #5660

## Problem

When using Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) tools with
`requires_confirmation=True` or `external_execution=True`, PostgreSQL
storage fails with:

```
TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable
```

This occurs because `RunRequirement.created_at` (a `datetime` field) is
not serialized before being inserted into PostgreSQL JSONB columns. The
error prevents sessions from being saved, which causes `continue_run()`
to fail with "No runs found".

### Root Cause

The serialization chain was:
1. `AgentSession.to_dict()` calls `run.to_dict()` for each run
2. `RunOutput.to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` which processes
`requirements`
3. `asdict()` converts `RunRequirement` but preserves raw `datetime`
objects
4. PostgreSQL JSONB insert fails because `datetime` is not
JSON-serializable

SQLite worked because it uses `CustomJSONEncoder` which handles
`datetime`, but PostgreSQL passes dicts directly to SQLAlchemy's JSONB
type.

## Solution

Add explicit serialization for `RunRequirement`:

1. **`RunRequirement.to_dict()`** - Serializes `created_at` to ISO 8601
string
2. **`RunRequirement.from_dict()`** - Reconstructs from stored dict,
parsing ISO strings back to `datetime`
3. **`RunOutput.to_dict()`** - Explicitly serializes `requirements`
using `RunRequirement.to_dict()`
4. **`RunOutput.from_dict()`** - Reconstructs `requirements` using
`RunRequirement.from_dict()`

## Changes

### `libs/agno/agno/run/requirement.py`

- Updated `__init__` to accept optional `id` and `created_at` parameters
for reconstruction
- Fixed `created_at` default to use `field(default_factory=...)` instead
of static value
- Added `to_dict()` method that serializes `created_at` to ISO 8601
string
- Added `from_dict()` classmethod that parses ISO strings back to
`datetime` objects

### `libs/agno/agno/run/agent.py`

- Added `"requirements"` to the exclusion list in `to_dict()`
- Added explicit serialization of `requirements` using `req.to_dict()`
- Added deserialization of `requirements` in `from_dict()`

## Backward Compatibility

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Missing `id` field | New UUID generated |
| Missing `tool_execution` | Placeholder created |
| Missing `created_at` | Falls back to `datetime.now()` |
| Sessions without requirements | Continue to work unchanged |

## Testing

- All existing unit tests pass
- End-to-end tested with PostgreSQL 16: session upsert and round-trip
work correctly
- `RunRequirement.to_dict()` produces JSON-serializable output
- Round-trip serialization preserves all fields including `id` and
`created_at`

requests that end with a malformed tool call. Also introduce the

chore: Release 2.3.13 (#5722)

# Changelog

## New Features:

- **AgentOS Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** → Introducing RBAC for
AgentOS (see the docs). This allows you to either automatically or
manually configure JWT-based authorization checks in AgentOS with the
following benefits:
- All traffic to your AgentOS would require a signed JWT token, with the
correct user permission scopes.
- Per-endpoint authorization → Based on the scopes inside the JWT token,
access is granted or denied to each endpoint as you choose. The required
scopes are configurable as well.
- Per-agent resource control → By setting specific scopes like
`agents:my-agent:read` you can control which agents can be run (i.e.
when calling `POST /agents/my-agent/runs` ) or which agents are returned
on read (i.e. when calling `GET /agents` or `GET /agents/{id}`). This
allows for full control over which users can use and see which agents,
and this extends to AgentOS. The same also applies to `Team` and
`Workflow`.
    - AgentOS UI compatibility to be released in the coming days.
    - **Note**: On the `JWTMiddleware` class:
- `secret_key` has been deprecated (although still supported) and it is
recommended to supply `verification_keys=[...]` going forward.
- `algorithm` default value changed from `HS256` to `RS256` to make
asymmetric keys the default (better suited for production cases).

chore: v2.3.14 (#5746)

# Changelog

## New Features:

- **Reasoning Streaming**: Add support to stream reasoning chunks for
the case where `reasoning_model` is provided.
- **A2A interface endpoints:** Add new endpoints to our A2A interface.
You can now obtain the Agent Card for any of the available Agents, Teams
and Workflows. We also updated the endpoints to run your Agents, Teams
and Workflows to fit the updated protocol. See the
[docs](https://docs.agno.com/agent-os/interfaces/a2a/introduction).

## Improvements:

- **JSON Schema for Structured Outputs**: `output_schema` now accepts
JSON schemas in provider-specific formats, passed directly to the model
API without transformation. This gives users full control over
structured output configuration for OpenAI, Claude, and OpenAI-like
providers.
- **Persistence for errored runs**: Improved how all kind of errors are
handled during Agent and Team runs. Now an event representing the error
will always be emitted (in streaming scenarios). And the runs containing
errors will also always be persisted, when relevant.
- **Session names on AgentOS**: Minor improvements to what is shown as
the Session name in the AgentOS, considering the case of session with
`introduction` messages.
- **Milvus Search**: Added `search_parameters` to the search and
async_search methods of the Milvus vector database class.
- **AgentOS app reloading**: Add `reload_includes` and `reload_excludes`
to the `serve` function of AgentOS. Using these you can specify which
files the AgentOS app listens to to reload.
- **Default Gemini Embedder**: The default model ID for Gemini Embedder
class has now been updated to the latest gemini-embedding-001

## Bug Fixes:

- **BaseEval Improvement:** Improved handling of agent and team
parameters inside tool functions by using lazy imports, resolving a
warning during access.
- **Milvus filtering**: Fix an issue parsing search filters under
certain conditions when using the Milvus vector database.
- **Duplicate ID validation**: Agents, Teams or Workflows with
duplicated IDs are no longer allowed in AgentOS, to avoid unexpected
behavior.

subject: feat: workflows reconnection support via socket (#5787)
message:
feat: workflows reconnection support via socket (#5787)

## Summary

- Event Buffering: New `EventBuffer` stores workflow events in-memory
with indexing for seamless reconnection
- Connection Management: Enhanced `WebSocketManager` with some cleanup
- Reconnection API: New WebSocket actions (`reconnect`, `catch_up`,
`replay`) for different reconnection scenarios.

### WebSocket Reconnection Scenarios

| Scenario | Action | Workflow State | Behavior |
|----------|--------|----------------|----------|
| **Catch-up** | `reconnect` | Running | Resume from `last_event_index`,
receive missed + new events |
| **Full Replay** | `reconnect` | Running | Send `last_event_index:
null` to get ALL events from start |
| **Completed Replay** | `reconnect` | Completed | Automatic full
replay, `last_event_index` ignored |

---

#### 🔄 `reconnect` + `catch_up` — Mid-execution catch-up

When a client disconnects during workflow execution and reconnects with
a specific `last_event_index`:

1. Client sends `reconnect` action with `last_event_index` (e.g., `42`)
2. Server responds with `catch_up` event containing:
   - `missed_events`: Number of events client missed
   - `current_event_count`: Total events so far
   - `status`: `"running"` or `"completed"`
3. Server streams all missed events (from `last_event_index + 1`)
4. Server sends `subscribed` event when caught up
5. Client continues receiving new events in real-time

---

#### ⏪ `catch_up` — Full history replay (running workflows)

When reconnecting to a **RUNNING** workflow with `last_event_index:
null`:

1. Client sends `reconnect` action with `last_event_index: null` (or
omitted)
2. Server responds with `catch_up` event indicating full replay
3. Server streams ALL events from beginning (`event_index: 0`)
4. Server sends `subscribed` event when caught up
5. Client receives complete workflow history + subscribes to ongoing
events

> **Use case**: Perfect for clients that lost all state or need full
context.

---

#### 🎬 `replay` — Completed workflow replay

When reconnecting to a **COMPLETED** workflow:

1. Client sends `reconnect` action (any `last_event_index` value)
2. Server responds with `replay` event containing:
   - `status`: `"completed"`
   - `total_events`: Total number of events in workflow
   - `message`: Replay notification
3. Server streams entire workflow execution history
4. Connection closes after final `WorkflowCompleted` event

> **Note**: `last_event_index` parameter is ignored — full replay is
always sent.

New cookbook examples demonstrate reconnection scenarios:
- **01_workflow_websocket_reconnect.py**: Mid-execution reconnection
with catch-up
- **02_workflow_events_replay.py**: Completed workflow event replay
- **03_workflow_disruption_fully_catchup.py**: Full event replay from
start

fix: propagate stop flag from primitive inner steps to workflow (#5868)

## Summary

Fixes the issue where 'Early termination requested by condition step'
was logged but workflow continued to execute subsequent steps.

When a step inside a Condition returns stop=True, the Condition now
correctly propagates this flag to the workflow level, causing the entire
workflow to stop executing subsequent steps.

Previously, the Condition would detect the stop flag and break out of
its internal loop, but would return a StepOutput with stop=False,
causing the workflow to continue executing steps that should have been
skipped.

Changes:
- Modified execute(), execute_stream(), aexecute(), and
aexecute_stream() methods in Condition class to propagate stop flag from
inner steps
- Added 5 test cases to verify stop propagation in various scenarios:
  - Direct Condition execution
  - Condition in workflow (sync/async)
  - Streaming mode (sync/async)

subject: feat: dynamic headers for MCP tools (#5655)
message:
feat: dynamic headers for MCP tools (#5655)

This PR implements dynamic per-request header support for MCPTools,
enabling multi-tenant applications to pass user context (user IDs,
tenant IDs, access tokens) from `RunContext` to MCP servers.

**Closes #5568**


## Solution

Implemented `header_provider` callback parameter for MCPTools and
MultiMCPTools, following Google ADK Python's precedent. Headers are
generated dynamically from `RunContext` and cached per agent run (not
per tool call) for optimal performance.

### Key Features:

1. **Dynamic Header Generation:** Headers generated from `RunContext`
(user_id, session_id, metadata)
2. **Per-Run Session Caching:** One connection per agent run, reused
across tool calls
3. **Multi-Server Support:** Works with both `MCPTools` (single server)
and `MultiMCPTools` (multiple servers)
4. **Automatic Integration:** `RunContext` automatically injected by
Agent - no manual passing needed
5. **Type-Safe:** Full type hints throughout

### Session Lifecycle

```
Agent Run Starts
    ↓
header_provider(RunContext) generates headers
    ↓
Create session with merged headers
    ↓
Cache session by run_id
    ↓
Tool Call 1 → reuse cached session
Tool Call 2 → reuse cached session
Tool Call N → reuse cached session
    ↓
Agent Run Ends → cleanup session
```

## Use Cases Enabled

### 1. Multi-Tenancy
```python
# Different tenants get isolated data
await agent.arun("Get my orders", user_id="user1", metadata={"tenant_id": "tenant-a"})
await agent.arun("Get my orders", user_id="user2", metadata={"tenant_id": "tenant-b"})
# MCP server receives different X-Tenant-ID headers
```

### 2. Per-User Authentication
```python
# Forward OAuth tokens dynamically
await agent.arun(
    "Access protected resource",
    user_id="alice",
    metadata={"access_token": oauth_token}
)
# MCP server receives Access-Token header for authorization
```

### 3. Audit Logging
```python
# Track which user made which calls
await agent.arun("Delete record", user_id="admin", session_id="session-123")
# MCP server logs: user=admin, session=session-123 deleted record
```

### 4. Rate Limiting
```python
# MCP server can rate-limit per user
await agent.arun("Make API call", user_id="user123")
# MCP server checks X-User-ID header for rate limit quota
```

example

chore: v2.3.22 (#5914)

# Changelog

## New features

- **Agent Skills**: Introducing the `Skills` class, enabling you to
extend your Agents’ capabilities by providing specific skills, as
defined by Anthropic’s [Agent Skill
specification](https://agentskills.io/home). See the
[docs](https://docs.agno.com/basics/skills).
- **Dynamic headers for MCP**: You can now pass a `header_provider`
function to your MCPTools instances to generate dynamic headers when
calling MCP tools. This is useful for headers that need to change based
on context e.g. authorization tokens or user ids. See the
[docs](https://docs.agno.com/basics/tools/mcp/dynamic-headers).

## Improvements:

- **Reasoning models**: enable native reasoning for the following
reasoning models:
    - OpenAI GPT-5.1 and 5.2 models
    - New Gemini 3, 3.5 and deepthink model
    - New DeepSeek r1 and reasoner models.
- **JWT Middleware Audience**: Allow setting of the expected `audience`
for checking
- **MCP transport default**: The `MCPTools` class now defaults to
`StreamableHttp` as transport when connecting to external MCP servers.
- **Postgres DB**: Updates to the database session pooling logic and
handling of illegal characters in any strings to store.0
- **A2A Remote Agents**: Added support for `a2a` protocol when using
remote agents. The also means Google ADK agents can be used with AgentOS
as remote running agents. This feature is still in beta. See the
[docs](https://docs.agno.com/agent-os/remote-execution/overview).

## Bug Fixes:

- **Chunking:** Fixed paragraph and newline splitting in chunking
strategies.
- **Early Termination in Workflows:** Propagate `stop` flag from
primitive inner steps to workflow
- **Context compression for OpenAIResponses**: Update our
`CompressionManager` to work properly with any model using the
`OpenAIResponses` API.

subject: fix: AttributeError in get_session_name when run_input is a string (#5869)
message:
fix: AttributeError in get_session_name when run_input is a string (#5869)

## Summary
- Fixed AttributeError in `get_session_name()` function in
`agno/os/utils.py`
- Added proper type checking before calling `.get()` method on
`run_input`

## Problem
The function was attempting to call `.get("input_content")` on
`run_input` when it was a string, causing:
```
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
```

This occurred in the session retrieval endpoint:
```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/agno/os/routers/session/session.py", line 169, in get_sessions
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/agno/os/schema.py", line 192, in from_dict
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/agno/os/utils.py", line 348, in get_session_name
```

## Solution
Changed the type checking logic from:
```python
if run_input is not None:
    return run_input.get("input_content")
```

To:
```python
if isinstance(run_input, str):
    return run_input
if isinstance(run_input, dict):
    return run_input.get("input_content")
```

This matches the pattern used in the `get_run_input()` function in the
same file (lines 275-277).

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify that sessions with string input values can be retrieved
without errors

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code
integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that
can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by
mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and
surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or
issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files,
diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the
workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and
interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file
like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action
repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

PR to get started!

subject: Fix: DocumentChunking Now Properly Respects chunk_size Parameter (#5916)
message:
Fix: DocumentChunking Now Properly Respects chunk_size Parameter (#5916)

**Fixes #5915**

## Summary
Fixed a critical bug in `DocumentChunking` where paragraphs larger than
the specified `chunk_size` were added as whole chunks without splitting,
effectively ignoring the `chunk_size` constraint.

## Problem
The `DocumentChunking` class in
`libs/agno/agno/knowledge/chunking/document.py` only checked if adding a
new paragraph would exceed the chunk size limit, but never validated
whether individual paragraphs themselves exceeded the limit.

**Before:**
- Setting `chunk_size=100` with paragraphs of 400+ characters resulted
in chunks of 400+ characters
- The parameter was completely ignored for large paragraphs
- Resulted in inconsistent chunk sizes

**After:**
- Same configuration now produces chunks of ~100 characters each
- Oversized paragraphs are split by sentences to respect the chunk_size
- Consistent and predictable chunk sizes

## Changes Made

### `libs/agno/agno/knowledge/chunking/document.py`
- Added logic to detect when a paragraph exceeds `chunk_size`
- When detected, the paragraph is split by sentences using regex pattern
`(?<=[.!?])\s+`
- Each sentence is then processed to fit within the chunk_size
constraint
- Maintains proper chunk numbering and metadata throughout

message:
fix: gemini vertex ai file upload error (#5857)

## Bug Fix: Gemini Vertex AI File Upload Error

**Fixes:** #5843

### Problem

When try to upload files to Gemini via Vertex AI, the API returned a 400
error:

```
Unable to submit request because it must include at least one parts field
```

This occurred because file `Part` objects were being appended to the
wrong list during message formatting, resulting in an empty `parts`
field in the `Content` object sent to the API.

### Root Cause

In `_format_messages()` at line 797, file parts were incorrectly
appended to `formatted_messages` (which holds complete `Content`
objects) instead of `message_parts` (which holds individual `Part`
objects):

```python
# BEFORE (Bug):
if isinstance(file_content, Part):
    formatted_messages.append(file_content)  # ❌ Wrong list!

# AFTER (Fix):
if isinstance(file_content, Part):
    message_parts.append(file_content)  # ✅ Correct list!
```

### Changes

**File:** `libs/agno/agno/models/google/gemini.py`

1. ✅ **Line 797:** Changed `formatted_messages.append(file_content)` →
`message_parts.append(file_content)`
2. ✅ **Removed dead code:**
   - Line 675: Unused `file_content` variable declaration
- Lines 803-805: Unreachable `isinstance(file_content, GeminiFile)`
check

**Why the removed code was dead:**
- `_format_file_for_message()` returns `Optional[Part]`, never
`GeminiFile`
- The `isinstance(file_content, GeminiFile)` check could never be true

### Test Coverage

Added comprehensive integration tests following existing codebase
patterns:

**File:** `libs/agno/tests/integration/models/google/test_multimodal.py`

1. ✅ `test_file_input_bytes()` - Tests file upload with bytes content
2. ✅ `test_file_input_with_text_prompt()` - Tests file + text
combination

subject: fix: Allow empty string passwords for PDF decryption (#6053)
message:
fix: Allow empty string passwords for PDF decryption (#6053)

## Summary
- Fixed bug where empty string passwords (`""`) were incorrectly treated
as `None` due to Python's falsy evaluation
- Added unit tests for password handling in PDFReader (sync and async)

## Problem
PDFs can be encrypted with an empty user password and a non-empty owner
password. This is common for documents that are:
- Freely viewable (no password prompt to open)
- But have restricted editing/printing (requires owner password)

The previous code used `password or self.password` which treats `""` as
falsy, causing decryption to fail for these valid PDFs.

## Solution
Changed from:
```python
pdf_password = password or self.password
if not pdf_password:
```

To:
```python
pdf_password = self.password if password is None else password
if pdf_password is None:
```

This explicitly checks for `None` rather than relying on truthiness,
preserving empty strings as valid passwords.

## Test plan
- [x] Added 6 unit tests for password handling (sync and async variants)
- [x] Tests verify: empty password works, None falls back to instance,
explicit overrides instance
- [x] All existing PDF reader tests still pass

Fixes #6051

and upsert operations.

subject: fix: add additionalProperties: false to Cerebras JSON schemas (#6014)
message:
fix: add additionalProperties: false to Cerebras JSON schemas (#6014)

Fixes #6013

## Summary

Fixes a 422 validation error when using Cerebras models with structured
outputs (JSON schema format). The Cerebras API requires
`additionalProperties: false` to be explicitly set for all object types
in JSON schemas, but this was not being enforced.

## Problem

When using Cerebras models (e.g., `zai-glm-4.7`) with features that use
structured outputs (like session summaries), the API returns:

```
Error code: 422 - {
  'message': "'additionalProperties' is required to be supplied and set to false.",
  'type': 'invalid_request_error',
  'param': 'response_format',
  'code': 'wrong_api_format'
}
```

This occurs because Pydantic-generated JSON schemas don't automatically
include `additionalProperties: false` for object types, which Cerebras
requires for schema validation.

## Solution

- Added `_ensure_additional_properties_false()` method that recursively
sets `additionalProperties: false` for all object types in a JSON schema
- Applied this fix when processing `response_format` with `type:
"json_schema"` in `get_request_params()`
- Follows the same pattern already implemented in the Anthropic model
(`claude.py`)

## Changes

- Added `_ensure_additional_properties_false()` method to `Cerebras`
class
- Modified `get_request_params()` to call this method when processing
JSON schema response formats
- Ensures all nested object types have `additionalProperties: false` set
recursively

## Testing

This fix resolves the issue for:
- Session summary generation with Cerebras models
- Any structured outputs using JSON schema format with Cerebras
- Nested object schemas (recursively processed)

## Related

This follows the same pattern as the Anthropic implementation:
- `agno/models/anthropic/claude.py` lines 272-288

subject: fix: Python Closure Bug in team.py function `adelegate_task_to_members`  (#6067)
message:
fix: Python Closure Bug in team.py function `adelegate_task_to_members`  (#6067)

## Summary

Fixed a Python closure bug in `Team.adelegate_task_to_members()` where
loop variables were not properly captured in async function definitions,
causing all concurrent member agent runs to use the **last** member's
values instead of their respective values.

When `delegate_to_all_members=True` is set on a Team and the team runs
in async mode (e.g., inside a Workflow), the `adelegate_task_to_members`
function creates async closures inside a `for` loop. These closures
reference loop variables (`member_agent`, `member_agent_task`,
`history`, `member_agent_index`) without capturing them via default
arguments.

Since `asyncio.gather()` executes these closures **after** the loop
completes, all closures see the **final** loop values—resulting in every
agent appearing to be the last one.

Before:
```
    {
      "role": "tool",
      "content": "\"Agent Worker3: {"Reply 1"}Agent Worker3: {"Reply 2"}Agent Worker3: {"Reply 3"}\"",
      ...
      }
```
After:
```
    {
      "role": "tool",
      "content": "\"AgentWorker1: {"Reply 1"}Agent Worker2: {"Reply 2"}Agent Worker3: {"Reply 3"}\"",
      ...
    }
```

<summary>Minimal Reproduction Example</summary>


```python
import asyncio
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.team import Team
from agno.models.openai import OpenAIChat
from agno.workflow import Workflow
from agno.workflow.step import StepInput, StepOutput

model = OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o-mini")

# Create 3 distinct agents
def create_agent(name: str) -> Agent:
    return Agent(
        id=name,
        name=name,
        model=model,
        instructions=[f"You are {name}. Always start your response with 'I am {name}.'"],
    )

agents = [create_agent(f"Worker{i}") for i in range(1, 4)]

# Team with delegate_to_all_members=True
team = Team(
    id="TestTeam",
    name="Test Team",
    model=model,
    members=agents,
    delegate_to_all_members=True,
    instructions=["Delegate to all members and report their responses."],
)

# Wrap in workflow to trigger async execution
async def dummy_step(step_input: StepInput) -> StepOutput:
    return StepOutput(content="Start")

workflow = Workflow(
    id="TestWorkflow",
    name="TestWorkflow",
    steps=[dummy_step, team],
)

async def main():
    result = await workflow.arun(input="Say hello")
    print(result.content)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Before Fix (Buggy Output)

```
Agent Worker3: I am Worker3. Hello!
Agent Worker3: I am Worker3. Hello!
Agent Worker3: I am Worker3. Hello!
```

All 3 responses incorrectly show "Worker3" (the last agent).

### After Fix (Correct Output)

```
Agent Worker1: I am Worker1. Hello!
Agent Worker2: I am Worker2. Hello!
Agent Worker3: I am Worker3. Hello!
```

Now Each agent correctly identifies itself.

subject: fix: handle async generator exceptions gracefully like sync generators (#6108)
message:
fix: handle async generator exceptions gracefully like sync generators (#6108)

Previously, when an async generator tool raised an exception during
iteration, the error was re-raised which caused the entire agent to
crash. This fix changes the async generator exception handling to match
the sync generator behavior:

- Instead of re-raising the exception, set function_call.error to the
error message
- Set function_call_success to False
- Log the error with the function name for better debugging

This allows the agent to continue running and report the error to the
model, which can then decide how to proceed (e.g., retry, use a
different approach, or inform the user).

The sync generator handling (which was fixed in PR #5464) already does
this:
```python
except Exception as e:
    log_error(f"Error while iterating function result generator for {function_call.function.name}: {e}")
    function_call.error = str(e)
    function_call_success = False
```

The async generator handling now matches this pattern.
Fixes #6095

subject: fix: Perplexity streaming token metrics accumulation (#6058)
message: fix: Perplexity streaming token metrics accumulation (#6058) ## Summary Fixed incorrect token count reporting for Perplexity streaming responses. Perplexity's streaming API returns **cumulative** token counts in each chunk (1, 2, 3, ..., N), but Agno was accumulating these values, resulting in dramatically inflated token counts. **Example of the issue:** - Expected: 29 output tokens, 1,965 input tokens, 1,994 total tokens - Actual (before fix): 366 output tokens, 47,160 input tokens, 47,526 total tokens - Error magnitude: ~24x inflation This fix introduces a configurable flag `collect_metrics_on_completion` that allows models to defer metrics collection until the final chunk (when `finish_reason` is set), preventing incorrect accumulation of cumulative token counts. I used the finish_reason as not none. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Improvement - [ ] Model update - [ ] Other: --- ## Technical Details ### Root Cause Perplexity's streaming API violates the standard incremental streaming pattern by sending cumulative token counts in each chunk: ```python # Perplexity's behavior: Chunk 1: CompletionUsage(completion_tokens=1, prompt_tokens=1965, total_tokens=1966) Chunk 2: CompletionUsage(completion_tokens=2, prompt_tokens=1965, total_tokens=1967) Chunk 3: CompletionUsage(completion_tokens=3, prompt_tokens=1965, total_tokens=1968) ... Chunk N: CompletionUsage(completion_tokens=29, prompt_tokens=1965, total_tokens=1994) ``` Agno's base streaming logic accumulates these values using `Metrics.__add__()`: ```python stream_data.response_metrics += model_response_delta.response_usage ``` This results in summing cumulative counts: - Output tokens: 1+2+3+...+29 = 435 (should be 29) - Input tokens: 1965×24 = 47,160 (should be 1965) ### Solution Added a model-level configuration flag to control when metrics are collected: 1. **New property in `OpenAIChat`**: `collect_metrics_on_completion: bool = False` - Default: `False` (preserves existing behavior for all models) - Set to `True` for models with cumulative token counting (Perplexity) 2. **New method `_should_collect_metrics()`**: ```python def _should_collect_metrics(self, response: ChatCompletion) -> bool: if response.usage is None: return False if self.collect_metrics_only_on_last_chunk: choice = response.choices[-1] if choice and choice.finish_reason is not None: return True return True ``` 3. **Perplexity model override**: `collect_metrics_only_on_last_chunk: bool = True` ## Evidence: ### Before ### After **Verification with OpenAI client** (bypassing Agno): ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( api_key=os.environ.get("PERPLEXITY_API_KEY"), base_url="https://api.perplexity.ai" ) # Result: CompletionUsage(completion_tokens=470, prompt_tokens=8, total_tokens=478, ...) # ✓ Correctly shows final cumulative count ``` ### Related Issues This issue has been documented in the broader LLM ecosystem: - **LiteLLM Issue #8455**: "Fix incorrect streaming response of Perplexity API" - documents Perplexity returning cumulative content and metrics - **Perplexity Documentation**: Confirms that usage/token data arrives only in final chunks during streaming - **Agno Issue #2310**: "Total token metrics at the end of the run does not reflect all the tokens used" ### Files Changed - `libs/agno/agno/models/openai/chat.py`: - Added `collect_metrics_only_on_last_chunk` property - Added `_should_collect_metrics()` method - Modified `_parse_provider_response()` to use new check - Modified `_parse_provider_response_delta()` to use new check - `libs/agno/agno/models/perplexity/perplexity.py`: - Set `collect_metrics_only_on_last_chunk = True` --- ## Checklist - [x] Code complies with style guidelines - [x] Ran format/validation scripts (`./scripts/format.sh` and `./scripts/validate.sh`) - [x] Self-review completed - [x] Documentation updated (comments, docstrings) - [ ] Examples and guides: Relevant cookbook examples have been included or updated (if applicable) - [x] Tested in clean environment - [x] Tests added/updated (if applicable) --- ## Additional Notes ### Backward Compatibility - ✅ **Fully backward compatible**: Default value is `False`, preserving existing behavior - ✅ **Only affects Perplexity**: Other OpenAI-compatible models unchanged - ✅ **No breaking changes**: Existing code continues to work without modification ### Testing Recommendations 1. **Verify Perplexity streaming**: ```python memory_db = InMemoryDb() agent = Agent(model=Perplexity(id="sonar"), db=memory_db, debug_mode=True) response = agent.run("Your query", stream=True) for chunk in response: pass metrics = agent.get_session_metrics() # Verify metrics show correct token counts, not inflated values ``` 2. **Verify OpenAI still works**: ```python agent = Agent(model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o-mini")) response = agent.run("Your query", stream=True) # Verify metrics are still collected correctly ``` 3. **Compare with direct API call**: - Use OpenAI client directly against Perplexity API - Compare final token counts with Agno's reported metrics - Should match exactly ### Future Considerations Other OpenAI-compatible providers may exhibit similar cumulative counting behavior. If reported, they can easily be fixed by setting `collect_metrics_on_completion = True` in their model class. ### Cost Implications This fix has **critical cost tracking implications**: - Incorrect token counts lead to inaccurate cost calculations - 24x inflation could cause billing discrepancies - Essential for production usage tracking and budgeting --------- Co-authored-by: u799fedb41af0b1cd Co-authored-by: uaf08fa645d56f244

subject: [feat] Support Excel files in Knowledge (#5862)
message:
[feat] Support Excel files in Knowledge (#5862)

## Summary
Adds first-class Excel (.xlsx/.xls) file ingestion for Knowledge by
routing spreadsheets to the CSV reader and parsing workbooks per-sheet.

## Rationale
Excel is treated as a spreadsheet/tabular source similar to CSV for
Knowledge ingestion. `CSVReader` already provides row-oriented text
extraction and integrates with existing chunking strategies (e.g.
`RowChunking`), so routing `.xlsx/.xls` through it keeps behavior
consistent and avoids introducing a new reader key / API surface. If we
later need richer spreadsheet semantics (formulas, formatting, table
region detection), we can extract a dedicated `ExcelReader`.

## Changes

### Core Excel Support
- Parse `.xlsx` via openpyxl and `.xls` via xlrd in CSVReader
- Each sheet becomes a separate Document with metadata (`sheet_name`,
`sheet_index`)
- Rows become content lines in CSV-like format
- Route `.xlsx`/`.xls` (+ common MIME types) to the csv reader in
ReaderFactory
- Add openpyxl/xlrd to the existing `agno[csv]` extra

### Bug Fixes for Edge Cases
- **Boolean handling**: xlrd returns booleans as `1`/`0` integers; added
`_convert_xls_cell_value()` to convert to proper `True`/`False`
- **Multiline content**: Cells with embedded newlines (`\n`, `\r`,
`\r\n`) would break row parsing; now normalized to spaces
- **CSV consistency**: Applied same normalization to CSV path (cells can
have embedded newlines too)
- **Trailing newline**: Both CSV and Excel paths now use
`"\n".join(lines)` pattern (no trailing newline)

### Other
- Fix `agno[memori]` extra to depend on `memori==3.0.5` (instead of
`memorisdk==3.0.5`)

chore: Release 2.4.1 (#6109)

# Changelog

## New Features:

- **N1N Model Provider:** Added [n1n.ai](http://n1n.ai/) as an
OpenAI-compatible provider.
- **Knowledge:** Added first-class Excel ingestion `(.xlsx/.xls)` by
routing spreadsheets through the existing CSV reader, parsing workbooks
per sheet into separate documents with sheet metadata.
- **Github/Sharepoint support:** Added functionality in SDK and on API
to support files in private github and sharepoint repos to be added to
Knowledge.

## Improvements:

- **Streaming metrics:** Add `collect_metrics_on_completion` flag to
only collect metrics from the final chunk.
- **Interfaces:** Prevent errors on interfaces from ending up to the
user facing message.

## Bug Fixes:

- **CustomEvent**: Add `tool_call_id` to trace events back to their
originating tool calls.
- **Knowledge metadata:** Fixed to properly propogate metdata filters
while using knowledge
- **Cerebras Model Provider:** Fixed a 422 validation error when using
Cerebras models with structured outputs (JSON schema format).
- **Team task delegation:** Fixed a Python closure bug
in `Team.adelegate_task_to_members()` where loop variables were not
properly captured in async function definitions, causing all concurrent
member agent runs to use the **last** member's values instead of their
respective values.
- **Async generator tools:** Handle async generator iteration exceptions
gracefully by capturing the error on the tool call instead of
re-raising, so the agent can continue and the model can decide how to
proceed.

fix: remove hasattr caching in async db drivers preventing table creation (#6128)

## Summary

Tables were not being created when using `AsyncSqliteDb`,
`AsyncPostgresDb`, `AsyncMySQLDb`, and `FirestoreDb`.
The `_get_table` method used `hasattr()` checks to cache table
references, but when first called with `create_table_if_not_found=False`
(during read operations), None would be cached. Subsequent calls with
`create_table_if_not_found=True` would return the cached `None` instead
of creating the table.

Removed the `hasattr` checks to match the behavior of sync drivers,
ensuring tables are created when needed.

fix: Fixed OpenAIEmbedder to pass the dimensions parameter for third-party OpenAI-compatible embedding APIs. (#6143)

## Summary
Fixed `OpenAIEmbedder` to pass the `dimensions` parameter for
third-party OpenAI-compatible embedding APIs.Related to #5525

  ## Problem
When using third-party OpenAI-compatible embedding APIs (like DashScope,
Azure OpenAI, etc.), the `dimensions` parameter was only passed when the
model ID started with `text-embedding-3`. This caused dimension mismatch
errors for third-party APIs.

  ## Solution
Changed the condition to also pass `dimensions` when using a custom
`base_url`:
  ```python
if self.id.startswith("text-embedding-3") or self.base_url is not None:
      req["dimensions"] = self.dimensions
```
  This maintains backward compatibility with older OpenAI models like text-embedding-ada-002 which don't support the dimensions parameter.

subject: feat: Knowledge Excel Reader (#6129)
message:
feat: Knowledge Excel Reader (#6129)

## Summary

Introduces a dedicated `ExcelReader` class, separating Excel file
handling from `CSVReader` for cleaner architecture and proper dependency
management.

---

## The Problem

Previously, `CSVReader` handled both CSV and Excel files, creating
issues:

```python
# Before: CSVReader doing too much
from agno.knowledge.reader.csv_reader import CSVReader

reader = CSVReader()
reader.read("data.csv")   # CSV handling
reader.read("data.xlsx")  # Excel handling - why is this in CSVReader?
reader.read("data.xls")   # Legacy Excel - also here?
```

**Issues:**
1. **Confusing API**: Users expect `CSVReader` to handle CSV, not Excel

---

## The Solution

Dedicated readers with clear responsibilities:

```python
# After: Clean separation
from agno.knowledge.reader.csv_reader import CSVReader
from agno.knowledge.reader.excel_reader import ExcelReader

# CSV files → CSVReader
csv_reader = CSVReader()
docs = csv_reader.read("data.csv")

# Excel files → ExcelReader  
excel_reader = ExcelReader()
docs = excel_reader.read("report.xlsx")

# With sheet filtering (Excel-specific feature)
excel_reader = ExcelReader(sheets=["Sales", "Q4"])
docs = excel_reader.read("quarterly_report.xlsx")
```

**ReaderFactory auto-routes by extension:**
```python
from agno.knowledge.reader.reader_factory import ReaderFactory

# Automatic format detection
reader = ReaderFactory.get_reader_for_extension(".xlsx")  # → ExcelReader
reader = ReaderFactory.get_reader_for_extension(".csv")   # → CSVReader
```

---

## ExcelReader Features

```python
from agno.knowledge.reader.excel_reader import ExcelReader

# Filter specific sheets by name or index
reader = ExcelReader(sheets=["Sales", 2])  # "Sales" sheet + 3rd sheet

# Skip hidden sheets (default: True)
reader = ExcelReader(skip_hidden_sheets=True)

# Include empty sheets (default: False)
reader = ExcelReader(include_empty_sheets=True)

# Disable row chunking for raw content
reader = ExcelReader(chunk=False)
docs = reader.read("workbook.xlsx")
# → One Document per sheet with full content
```

**Output document structure:**
```python
# With chunking (default) - one Document per row
doc.meta_data = {
    "sheet": "Sales",
    "row": 2,
    "workbook": "quarterly_report"
}
doc.content = "product: Widget, revenue: 50000, region: North"

# Without chunking - one Document per sheet
doc.content = "product, revenue, region\nWidget, 50000, North\n..."
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `libs/agno/agno/knowledge/reader/excel_reader.py` | **New** -
Dedicated Excel reader (280 lines) |
| `libs/agno/agno/knowledge/reader/spreadsheet_utils.py` | **New** -
Shared cell conversion utilities |
| `libs/agno/agno/knowledge/reader/csv_reader.py` | Removed Excel code,
now CSV-only |
| `libs/agno/agno/knowledge/reader/reader_factory.py` | Routes
.xlsx/.xls → ExcelReader |
| `libs/agno/pyproject.toml` | New `[excel]` extra |

---

## New Cookbooks

| Cookbook | Demonstrates |
|----------|--------------|
| `excel_reader.py` | Basic usage with Knowledge + Agent |
| `excel_multi_sheet.py` | Multi-sheet workbooks |
| `excel_employee_analytics.py` | Large dataset (1000 rows) |
| `excel_financials.py` | Financial data with dates/decimals |
| `excel_enterprise_edge_cases.py` | Unicode, special characters |
| `excel_legacy_xls.py` | Legacy .xls format |
| `agentos_excel_knowledge.py` | AgentOS REST API integration |

Consolidates two separate Claude Code workflows into a single workflow
file with two jobs:

| Potential double API usage | Mutually exclusive job conditions |

fix: pass dependencies to RunContext in Workflows (#6172)

## Summary

When using `JWTMiddleware` with `dependencies_claims` to inject user
data from JWT tokens, the dependencies were correctly available to agent
tools when calling the agent directly via `/agents/{agent_id}/runs`, but
not when the same agent ran as part of a workflow via
`/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs`.

Tools accessing `run_context.dependencies` would receive `None` instead
of the extracted JWT claims.

### Root Cause
The `Workflow.run()` and `Workflow.arun()` methods did not have a
`dependencies` parameter in their signatures. While `Agent.run()`
already supported this parameter, workflows were missing it. The JWT
middleware correctly extracted dependencies and passed them via kwargs,
but they were never mapped to the RunContext.

## Summary

Fixes a bug where the overlap section in `DocumentChunking` used a stale

subject: fix: Add fallback chunk ID generation for documents without id/name (#6018)
message:
fix: Add fallback chunk ID generation for documents without id/name (#6018)

## Summary
- **Before:** `Document(content="...")` without `id` or `name` produced
chunks with `id=None`
- **After:** Same documents produce chunks with deterministic IDs like
`chunk_a8f3b2c1d4e5_1`
- Adds `_generate_chunk_id()` method to base `ChunkingStrategy` class
with fallback chain
- Fixes vector DB insert failures, `skip_if_exists` deduplication, and
duplicate entries on re-indexing
- All 8 chunking strategies now share consistent ID generation logic
- Backward compatible: documents with `id` or `name` unchanged

## Motivation
- Vector databases require unique, non-null IDs for upsert operations
- `skip_if_exists` deduplication breaks when all chunks have `id=None`
- Re-indexing the same document creates duplicate entries instead of
updating
- Common scenario: text from APIs, user input, or web scraping often
lacks identifiers
- This is a foundational fix that unblocks reliable knowledge ingestion
workflows

**Repro (before fix):**
1. Create document: `doc = Document(content="Some long text...")`
2. Chunk it: `chunks = FixedSizeChunking(chunk_size=100).chunk(doc)`
3. Check ID: `chunks[0].id` → `None`
4. Insert to vector DB → fails or creates duplicates

## Changes
- `strategy.py`: Added `_generate_chunk_id(document, chunk_number,
content, prefix)` method to base class
- `fixed.py`: Uses `self._generate_chunk_id()` instead of inline ID
logic
- `document.py`: Uses `self._generate_chunk_id()` in all chunk creation
paths
- `markdown.py`: Uses `self._generate_chunk_id()` including new
`_split_large_section()` code paths
- `recursive.py`: Uses `self._generate_chunk_id()` instead of inline ID
logic
- `code.py`: Uses `self._generate_chunk_id()` for code chunks
- `semantic.py`: Uses `self._generate_chunk_id()` for semantic chunks
- `agentic.py`: Uses `self._generate_chunk_id()` for agentic chunks
- `row.py`: Uses `self._generate_chunk_id()` with `prefix="row"` for
`_row_` separator
- `test_chunk_id_generation.py`: New test file with 13 tests covering
fallback chain, determinism, and edge cases
- No API changes; all changes are internal implementation details

## Design / Reasoning
The solution adds a single method to the base `ChunkingStrategy` class
that all 8 chunking strategies inherit. This ensures consistent ID
generation across the codebase without duplicating logic.

The fallback chain (`document.id` → `document.name` → content hash) was
chosen because it preserves existing behavior for documents that already
have identifiers while providing a deterministic fallback for those that
don't.

MD5 was selected for hashing because it's fast, deterministic, and the
12-character truncation provides sufficient uniqueness for chunk
deduplication (16^12 = 281 trillion combinations). Security isn't a
concern here since we're generating identifiers, not protecting secrets.
The `# nosec B324` annotation documents this intentional choice.

**Alternative considered:** Using UUID4 for missing IDs. Rejected
because UUIDs are non-deterministic—re-chunking the same content would
produce different IDs, breaking `skip_if_exists` and causing duplicates.

**Invariants preserved:**
- Same content always produces same chunk ID (deterministic)
- Different content produces different chunk IDs (unique)
- Existing documents with `id` or `name` get unchanged ID format

## Edge cases
- **Empty content:** Returns empty list (no chunks created, no ID
needed)
- **Unicode/emoji content:** Hashes correctly via UTF-8 encoding
- **Very long content:** Only first chunk's content is hashed, not
entire document
- **RowChunking:** Uses `_row_` prefix to distinguish from other
chunking strategies (e.g., `doc_row_1` vs `doc_1`)
- **Overlap sections:** ID generation in overlap paths is unchanged
(separate bug fixed in PR #6159)

## Testing
```bash
# Run all chunking tests (78 tests)
cd libs/agno && uv run pytest tests/unit/knowledge/chunking/ -v

# Run chunk ID specific tests (13 tests)
cd libs/agno && uv run pytest tests/unit/knowledge/chunking/test_chunk_id_generation.py -v

# Run all knowledge tests (308 tests)
cd libs/agno && uv run pytest tests/unit/knowledge/ -v

# Manual verification

chunks = FixedSizeChunking(chunk_size=100).chunk(doc)
print(f'Chunk ID: {chunks[0].id}')  # Should print: chunk_XXXXXXXXXXXX_1
"
```

`unstructured` version 0.18.31 was released today (Jan 27, 2026 at 15:33

```
`llvmlite` (v0.36.0) was included because `agno[tests]` depends on `unstructured` (v0.18.31) which depends on `numba`
```

|-------------------|------------------------|--------|
| 09:17 | 0.18.27 | ✅ Pass |
| 22:46 | 0.18.31 | ❌ Fail |

PyPI release times:
- `unstructured==0.18.27`: Jan 9, 15:51 UTC
- `unstructured==0.18.31`: Jan 27, 15:33 UTC

Pin `unstructured<0.18.31` in the `markdown` extras to use the last

subject: fix: explicitly show <scripts>none</scripts> in skills system prompt (#6311)
message:
fix: explicitly show <scripts>none</scripts> in skills system prompt (#6311)

## Summary

Fixes #6304

When a skill has no scripts, the system prompt now explicitly shows
`<scripts>none</scripts>` instead of omitting the tag entirely. This
prevents less capable models from confusing reference files with
scripts.

### Problem

When using skills with certain models (e.g.,
Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507), the agent would incorrectly call
`get_skill_script` with a reference file path (like `run_task.md`) when
the skill had no actual scripts. This happened because:

1. The `<scripts>` tag was simply **omitted** when a skill had no
scripts
2. Models had to **infer** from the missing tag that no scripts existed
3. Less capable models saw reference files and mistakenly tried to use
them as scripts

### Solution

1. **Explicit indication**: Now shows `<scripts>none</scripts>` instead
of omitting the tag
2. **Clear instruction**: Added guidance that references are NOT
executable and `get_skill_script` should not be called when scripts is
"none"

### Before

```xml
<skill>
  <name>my-skill</name>
  <description>A documentation-only skill</description>
  <references>run_task.md</references>
</skill>
```

### After

```xml
<skill>
  <name>my-skill</name>
  <description>A documentation-only skill</description>
  <scripts>none</scripts>
  <references>run_task.md</references>
</skill>
```

Plus added instruction:
> **IMPORTANT**: References are documentation files (NOT executable).
Only use `get_skill_script` when `<scripts>` lists actual script files.
If `<scripts>none</scripts>`, do NOT call `get_skill_script`.

### Testing

- Reproduced the issue with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 via OpenRouter
- Verified fix prevents model from confusing references with scripts
- Added unit test `test_get_system_prompt_shows_none_when_no_scripts`
- All 44 skills tests pass

subject: fix: handle text file formats correctly in document messages (#6329)
message:
fix: handle text file formats correctly in document messages (#6329)

## Summary

Fix `_format_file_for_message` in the Claude model adapter to correctly
handle text-based file formats (CSV, JSON, HTML, Python, etc.).

**Not a breaking change** — every text file type was broken before. PDF
files (the only working type) are unaffected.

### Example: CSV file uploaded via Slack

A user uploads `report.csv` with content `name,revenue\nAcme,50000`. The
Slack router creates `File(content=b"...", mime_type="text/csv")`.

**OLD code** (broken):
```
Step 1: base64_encode(bytes) → "bmFtZSxyZXZlbnVlCkFjbWUsNTAwMDA="
Step 2: mime_mapping.get("text/csv", "base64") → "base64" (text/csv wasn't in mapping)
Step 3: Send: {"type": "base64", "media_type": "text/csv", "data": "bmFtZSxyZXZlbnVl..."}
```
Two problems:
1. `media_type: "text/csv"` — SDK only accepts `"application/pdf"` for
base64 sources
2. Model receives base64 gibberish, not readable CSV

For `text/plain` it was worse — mapping returned `"text"`, so base64
gibberish was sent as the "plain text" data.

**NEW code** (fixed):
```
Step 1: raw_bytes = b"name,revenue\nAcme,50000"
Step 2: mime_mapping.get("text/csv") → "text" (text/csv now in mapping)
Step 3: raw_bytes.decode("utf-8") → "name,revenue\nAcme,50000"
Step 4: Send: {"type": "text", "media_type": "text/plain", "data": "name,revenue\nAcme,50000"}
```

| | Old | New |
|--|-----|-----|
| CSV content sent to model | `bmFtZSxyZXZlbnVl...` |
`name,revenue\nAcme,50000\n...` |
| Source type | `"base64"` (wrong for text) | `"text"` (correct) |
| media_type | `"text/csv"` (API rejects) | `"text/plain"` (API accepts)
|

### Why hardcoded `"text/plain"`?

The Anthropic SDK enforces strict literal types:
- `PlainTextSourceParam`: `media_type: Literal["text/plain"]` — the only
option for text
- `Base64PDFSourceParam`: `media_type: Literal["application/pdf"]` — the
only option for binary

All text content goes through PlainTextSource regardless of original
MIME type. The model determines the format from the actual content, not
the MIME type.

Full reference ->
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files
### Changes

- Expanded `mime_mapping` to cover all text MIME types from
`File.valid_mime_types()`
- Read bytes first, then conditionally encode based on MIME type (was
encoding before checking)
- Added text source branch to Case 3 (bytes content) — previously always
used base64

[feat] v2.5 Phase 1 — Agent/Team refactor and baseline (#6429)

## Summary

Foundational v2.5 refactor that decomposes the monolithic `Agent` and
`Team` classes into focused, maintainable submodules, centralizes run
options, removes dead code, and adds a new DB migration.

### Agent module decomposition
The 12k+ line `agent.py` has been split into focused submodules while
preserving the public API surface:
- `_run.py` — core run loop (sync + async)
- `_messages.py` — message construction and formatting
- `_response.py` — response processing and streaming
- `_session.py` — session lifecycle management
- `_storage.py` — persistence and storage operations
- `_tools.py` — tool registration and management
- `_managers.py` — model, memory, and knowledge managers
- `_hooks.py` — lifecycle hooks (pre/post run, tool call, etc.)
- `_cli.py` — CLI interaction utilities
- `_default_tools.py` — built-in tool definitions
- `_init.py` — initialization and configuration
- `_telemetry.py` — telemetry and tracing
- `_utils.py` — shared utilities
- `_run_options.py` — centralized `RunOptions` dataclass

### Team module decomposition
Same decomposition pattern applied to `team.py`, producing a parallel
set of focused submodules (`_run.py`, `_messages.py`, `_response.py`,
`_session.py`, `_storage.py`, `_tools.py`, `_managers.py`, `_hooks.py`,
`_cli.py`, `_default_tools.py`, `_init.py`, `_telemetry.py`,
`_utils.py`, `_run_options.py`).

### Centralized run options
New `RunOptions` dataclass for both Agent and Team that consolidates the
many parameters previously passed through run function signatures,
improving maintainability and reducing parameter drift.

### Dead code removal
Removed ~90 dead wrapper methods from the `Agent` class that were no
longer serving a purpose.

### Call convention refactor
Refactored both agent and team modules to use direct lazy sibling
imports instead of indirect call patterns, improving code clarity and
traceability.

### DB migration v2_5_0
New database migration (`v2_5_0`) with dynamic PK constraint name
detection (no hardcoded constraint names), supporting Postgres, MySQL,
SQLite, and SingleStore schemas. Adds primary key constraint to
`session_id`.

V2.5 phase4 rb (#6514)

## Summary

Adds the human approvals system for HITL (human-in-the-loop) tool runs.
This is **Phase 4** of the v2.5 release, built on top of v2.5-phase3
(core refactor, team features, and scheduler infrastructure).

Tools decorated with `@h7c9bbe5ec9b3fb77(requires_approval=True)` now create
persistent approval records when a run pauses. External systems (UIs,
APIs, automation) can list, inspect, filter, and resolve these approvals
via REST endpoints — providing a queryable "approval inbox" for
production workflows requiring human sign-off (deployments, deletions,
bulk operations, etc.).

### What's included

**Approval data model and persistence**
- New `Approval` dataclass (`libs/agno/agno/db/schemas/approval.py`)
with full lifecycle fields: status, source type, context, resolution
metadata
- 6 CRUD methods added to `BaseDb` and `AsyncBaseDb`: `create_approval`,
`get_approval`, `get_approvals` (with filtering/pagination),
`update_approval` (with atomic status guard), `delete_approval`,
`get_pending_approval_count`
- Full implementations for both PostgreSQL (`postgres.py`,
`async_postgres.py`) and SQLite (`sqlite.py`, `async_sqlite.py`)
- DDL schemas for `agno_approvals` table in both database backends

**Tool decorator and model layer**
- `@h7c9bbe5ec9b3fb77(requires_approval=True)` parameter on the tool decorator;
implies `requires_confirmation=True` when no other HITL flag is set
- `requires_approval` field on `Function` model, included in
serialization
- `requires_approval` propagated through `ToolExecution` for all HITL
paths (confirmation, user_input, external_execution) in both sync and
async model flows
- Internal keys (`requires_approval`, `requires_confirmation`,
`external_execution`) stripped from tool dicts sent to non-OpenAI
providers

**Agent and team integration**
- All 4 agent pause handlers (`handle_agent_run_paused`, `_stream`,
`ahandle_agent_run_paused`, `_stream`) call `create_approval_from_pause`
/ `acreate_approval_from_pause`
- All 4 team pause handlers in `_hooks.py` do the same
- Core logic in `libs/agno/agno/run/approval.py`: checks both
`run_response.tools` (agent-level) and `run_response.requirements`
(team-level, where member tools propagate via requirements)

**REST API**
- 5 endpoints: `GET /approvals` (list with filtering), `GET
/approvals/count`, `GET /approvals/{id}`, `POST
/approvals/{id}/resolve`, `DELETE /approvals/{id}`
- Pydantic request/response schemas
- OAuth scope mappings (`approvals:read`, `approvals:write`,
`approvals:delete`)
- Approval router registered in `AgentOS` alongside the schedule router

**Cookbooks**
- `approval_basic.py` — Agent with approval-required tool
- `approval_async.py` — Async variant
- `approval_team.py` — Team member's tool triggers team-level approval
- `approval_list_and_resolve.py` — Full lifecycle with filtering,
approval/rejection, double-resolve guard
- `README.md` and `TEST_LOG.md`

**Cleanup**
- Removed `cookbook/02_agents/callable_factories/` (4 files, moved
elsewhere in prior phase)

## Additional Notes

This is the 4th stacked PR in the v2.5 release train:
- Phase 1: Core agent/team refactor

Key design decisions:
- Approval creation is silently skipped if the DB doesn't support it
(`NotImplementedError` catch), so existing setups without the new table
are unaffected
- The resolve endpoint uses an atomic `expected_status` guard to prevent
double-resolution race conditions
- `requires_approval` implies `requires_confirmation` but is a separate
concern — it controls persistence, not the pause behavior itself
- Team-level detection checks both `tools` and `requirements` to catch
member agent approval-requiring tools propagated via the team's
requirement system

subject: fix: restore missing v2.5 fields in SqliteDb/PostgresDb from_dict (#6531)
message:
fix: restore missing v2.5 fields in SqliteDb/PostgresDb from_dict (#6531)

## Summary

- `SqliteDb.from_dict()` and `PostgresDb.from_dict()` were missing 4
fields added in v2.5: `learnings_table`, `schedules_table`,
`schedule_runs_table`, and `approvals_table`
- Custom table names silently revert to defaults when agents are
restored from DB (e.g. via AgentOS API after a server restart)
- This leads to split-brain data where new writes go to default tables
while existing data remains in the custom tables

## Root Cause

`BaseDb.from_dict()` correctly includes all 4 fields, but `SqliteDb` and
`PostgresDb` override `from_dict()` without calling `super()` and
omitted the 4 fields that were added across PRs #5897, the v2.5 Phase 3
scheduler, and #6514.

## Who is affected

Users who customize DB table names in multi-agent setups (e.g.
`SqliteDb(learnings_table="support_learnings")`) and whose agents go
through the DB restoration path in AgentOS.

Users with default table names are **not** affected (the defaults match
anyway).

## Production Flow Where This Breaks

```
curl POST /agents/support-agent/run
  → router.py:253       get_agent_by_id(agent_id, os.agents, os.db)
  → os/utils.py:536     agent NOT in os.agents → fall back to DB
  → agent.py:1630       Agent.from_dict(cfg, registry)
  → _storage.py:762     from_dict() reconstructs Agent from config dict
  → _storage.py:775     db_from_dict(db_data)
  → db/utils.py:170     SqliteDb.from_dict(data)   ← BUG: 4 fields dropped
```

This path triggers when:
1. **Server restart** — agent not in memory, must be loaded from DB
2. **Dynamic agent creation via API** — agent created through API, not
in startup list
3. **A2A interface** — external agents call in, target loaded from DB
4. **Version pinning** — specific version requested, loaded from DB

### What happens step by step

**Step 1:** User creates agent with custom table names
```python
db = SqliteDb(
    db_file="app.db",
    learnings_table="support_learnings",
    approvals_table="support_approvals",
)
agent = Agent(id="support", db=db, ...)
```

**Step 2:** Agent runs, config saved to DB via
`_storage.to_dict(agent)`. The JSON correctly contains all custom table
names:
```json
{"db": {"type": "sqlite", "learnings_table": "support_learnings", "approvals_table": "support_approvals", ...}}
```

**Step 3:** Server restarts. A curl request arrives. AgentOS calls
`get_agent_by_id()`, agent isn't in memory, falls back to DB, loads the
JSON, calls `SqliteDb.from_dict(data)`.

**Step 4 (the bug):** `from_dict()` reads 14 of 18 fields. The 4 v2.5
fields are silently dropped. The restored `SqliteDb` uses defaults:
- `support_learnings` → `agno_learnings`
- `support_approvals` → `agno_approvals`
- `support_schedules` → `agno_schedules`
- `support_schedule_runs` → `agno_schedule_runs`

**Step 5 (the consequence):** The restored agent reads/writes to the
wrong tables. No error is logged. No warning. The agent appears to work
but:
- Accumulated learnings are invisible (wrong table)
- Pending approvals are invisible (wrong table)  
- New data goes to default tables, creating split-brain state

## Reproduction

```python
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.agent._storage import to_dict, from_dict
from agno.db.sqlite.sqlite import SqliteDb
from agno.models.openai import OpenAIChat

# Create agent with custom tables
db = SqliteDb(db_file="/tmp/test.db", learnings_table="custom_learnings")
agent = Agent(id="test", model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o-mini"), db=db)

# Simulate: agent.run() saves config → server restart → Agent.from_dict() restores
config = to_dict(agent)
restored = from_dict(Agent, data=config, registry=None)

# Before fix:
assert restored.db.learnings_table_name == "agno_learnings"    # silently wrong

# After fix:
assert restored.db.learnings_table_name == "custom_learnings"  # correct
```

## Adapters affected

| Adapter | Has `from_dict`? | In restoration path? | Fixed? |
|---------|-----------------|---------------------|--------|
| SqliteDb | Yes (override) | Yes | **Fixed** |
| PostgresDb | Yes (override) | Yes | **Fixed** |
| BaseDb | Yes (already correct) | N/A (abstract) | N/A |
| AsyncSqliteDb | No | No | N/A |
| AsyncPostgresDb | No | No | N/A |

The `db_from_dict()` dispatcher in `db/utils.py` only routes to
`SqliteDb` and `PostgresDb`. Other adapters (Mongo, MySQL, etc.) are not
in the restoration path.

feat: Release 2.5.0 (#6501)

# Changelog

## New Features

- **Team Execution Modes**: Introduced `TeamMode` enum with four
execution modes:
- `coordinate` (default): Supervisor pattern where the leader picks
members, crafts tasks, and synthesizes responses
- `route`: Router pattern where the leader routes to a specialist and
returns their response directly
- `broadcast`: Broadcast pattern where the leader delegates the same
task to all members simultaneously
- `tasks`: Autonomous task-based execution where the leader decomposes
goals into a shared task list
- **Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) for Teams**: Improved `RunRequirement`
system for paused runs with better support for:
    - Tool confirmation flows
    - User input collection with schema validation
    - External tool execution
- **Approval System**: New `@h9deb65b8788f41ff` decorator for human approval
workflows:
- `@h9deb65b8788f41ff(type="required")`: Blocking approval that pauses the run
until resolved via approvals API
- `@h9deb65b8788f41ff(type="audit")`: Non-blocking audit trail for
compliance/logging
- Persistent approval records with status tracking (pending, approved,
rejected, expired, cancelled)
    - Approvals API for listing, inspecting, and resolving approvals
- **Scheduler**: Cron-based scheduling for agents, teams, and workflows
with retry, timeout, and timezone support.
- **LearningMachine for Teams**: Added support for `LearningMachine` for
persistent learning.
- **Callable Factories for Tools, Knowledge, and Members**: Tools,
knowledge, and team members can now be defined as callable factories
that are resolved at runtime with access to `RunContext`. Supports
caching via `cache_callables` and custom cache keys for session-scoped
resolution.
- **Infra:** Adds support for AWS EFS
- **Knowledge Isolation**:
Added `isolate_vector_search flag` to Knowledge class. When enabled,
documents are tagged with `linked_to` metadata
during insert and searches filter by this tag,
allowing multiple Knowledge instances to share the same
vector database while maintaining isolated search results.
Defaults to `False` for backwards compatibility with existing data.

## Improvements

- **Agent/Team Refactor**: Major internal refactor of Agent and Team
classes for cleaner separation of concerns.

## Bug Fixes:

- **LanceDb Cloud:** Fixed `search()` to stop reopening the table; use
`.to_list()` instead of `.to_pandas()` in vector/hybrid/keyword search.
- **Primary key constraint:** Fixed `sessions`, `component_configs` and
`component_links` table to use primary key instead of
`_unique_constraints`.

## Breaking Changes

- **`store_history_messages` now defaults to `False`**: History messages
are no longer stored by default. This reduces unnecessary storage
overhead, improves privacy by not persisting conversation history unless
explicitly needed, and gives better control over storage costs. If you
rely on stored history, set `store_history_messages=True` explicitly.
- **Knowledge Uniqueness**: Knowledge instances now require a unique
combination of database, table, and knowledge name. Multiple Knowledge
instances cannot share the same table without distinct names to prevent
data conflicts.

refactor: Fail explicitly when header_provider is incompatible with transport (#5988)

## Fail explicitly when `header_provider` is incompatible with transport

### What changed

This PR introduces a **fail-fast validation** when a `header_provider`
is passed with an incompatible transport.

Previously, if a user supplied a `header_provider` that is not supported
by the selected transport (e.g. `stdio`), the code would:

- Silently set `self.header_provider = None`
- Log a warning
- Continue execution

This behavior can easily go unnoticed and lead to confusing situations
where headers appear to be ignored.

---

### New behavior

If a `header_provider` is explicitly provided and is incompatible with
the selected transport, we now **raise a `ValueError` immediately**.

```python
self.header_provider = None
if header_provider is not None:
    if not self._is_valid_header_provider(header_provider):
        raise ValueError(
            f"header_provider is not supported with '{self.transport}' transport. "
            "Use 'sse' or 'streamable-http' transport instead."
        )
    self.header_provider = header_provider
```

---

### Why this is needed

- Users who pass a `header_provider` explicitly expect it to be applied
- Silent fallback + warning logs are easy to miss
- Explicit failure makes misconfiguration obvious and easier to debug
- Aligns with standard configuration validation patterns

---

### Context

This PR is a follow-up to the earlier discussion in **PR #5930** (raised
while addressing **issue #5929**), where the silent fallback behavior
was identified.

In that discussion, it was agreed that an incompatible header_provider
should result in an explicit error rather than being silently ignored.
@h34f92773e8450c5d, also confirmed this approach on Discord, and this change
implements that agreed behavior.

---

### Impact

- No behavior change for valid configurations
- Invalid configurations now fail fast with a clear error message
- Improves developer experience and avoids silent misconfigurations

subject: fix: match include/exclude patterns against filename for directory scanning (#6455)
message:
fix: match include/exclude patterns against filename for directory scanning (#6455)

## Summary

Fixes #5230

When `add_content_async` (or `ainsert`) is called with a directory path
and `include=["*.go"]`, no files are matched despite the directory
containing `.go` files. The bug is in `_should_include_file` which uses
`fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern)` where `file_path` is a
full/relative path like `/home/user/project/src/main.go`. Since
`fnmatch`'s `*` wildcard does **not** match directory separators (`/`),
`*.go` only matches filenames without any directory component.

## Root Cause

```python
# Before: only matches files at the "root" level (no directories in path)
fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern)  # fnmatch("/path/to/file.go", "*.go") → False
```

## Fix

Match patterns against both the full path **and** the basename:

```python
file_name = os.path.basename(file_path)
fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern)
```

This way:

fix: prevent reasoning_content duplication across reasoning steps (#6438)

## Summary

Fixes #5948

The `reasoning_content` field in ReasoningStep events grows
exponentially with each step because it duplicates all previous content.

## Root Cause

In `update_reasoning_steps_in_run_response()`, the `reasoning_steps`
parameter contains ALL steps (including previous ones). The loop builds
`reasoning_content` from all of them, then APPENDS it to
`run_response.reasoning_content` which already contains content from
prior calls.

After step N, the reasoning_content contains N copies of step 1, N-1
copies of step 2, etc.

## Fix

Changed from append to direct assignment. Since `reasoning_steps`
already contains all steps, the loop output IS the complete reasoning
content. There's no need to append to existing content.

## Before
```
Step 4 reasoning_content: "step1 step2 step3 step1 step2 step3 step4"
```

## After
```
Step 4 reasoning_content: "step1 step2 step3 step4"
```

subject: [fix] HITL pause session state loss (#6495)
message:
[fix] HITL pause session state loss (#6495)

## Summary

HITL pause handlers silently drop `session_state` changes in both
**agent** and **team** modules.

### Why it happens — the code path

When an agent/team pauses for HITL, the flow goes through pause
handlers:

```
_run() / _run_stream() / _arun() / _arun_stream()
  └─ detects tool.is_paused
     └─ calls handle_*_run_paused(agent/team, run_response, session, ...)
        └─ calls cleanup_and_store(agent/team, run_response, session)
                                                              ↑
                                                   run_context NOT passed
```

Inside `cleanup_and_store`, `run_context` is always `None` during
pauses, so session_state is never persisted to DB.

### Impact

When a tool modifies `run_context.session_state` (e.g., adds an item to
a watchlist) and the agent/team then pauses for HITL confirmation, the
state changes are not persisted. After `continue_run()`, the session
loads stale state from DB.

### Fix

**Agent (8 call sites):**
- Added `run_context` param to all 4 pause handler signatures
- Forwarded to `cleanup_and_store` / `acleanup_and_store` at all 8 call
sites

**Team (18 call sites):**
- Added `run_context` param to all 4 team pause handlers in
`team/_hooks.py`
- Added `run_context` param + session_state persistence logic to
`_cleanup_and_store` / `_acleanup_and_store` in `team/_run.py`
- Forwarded `run_context` at all 18 call sites across `_run`,
`_run_stream`, `_arun`, `_arun_stream`, `continue_run_dispatch`,
`_continue_run`, `_continue_run_stream`, `_acontinue_run`,
`_acontinue_run_stream`

**Guard bug fix (agent + team):**
- Removed incorrect `session.session_data is not None` guard from
`run_response.session_state` assignment in all 4 cleanup functions. The
guard was a copy-paste artifact — it gated the return value on the DB
storage dict, but the source of truth is `run_context`, not
`session_data`. This caused `run_response.session_state` to be `None`
for legacy sessions with null `session_data`, even though the DB saved
correctly.

**Workflows:** Not affected — workflows don't have HITL pause handlers.
When a workflow step contains an agent that pauses, the pause is handled
at the agent level.

### Tests (38 total)

**Agent tests** (26 in `tests/unit/agent/test_run_regressions.py`):
- 12 HITL-specific: signature checks, forwarding
(sync/async/stream/async-stream), state persistence, backward compat,
null `session_data` edge cases

**Team tests** (12 in `tests/unit/team/test_team_run_regressions.py`,
new file):
- 1:1 mirror of agent HITL tests covering all the same variants

message:
fix: prevent race condition on run_context.output_schema in Parallel execution (#6609)

## Summary

Fixes a race condition on `run_context.output_schema` when `Parallel`
steps execute agents with different output schema types concurrently.

When `Parallel` passes the same `run_context` object by reference to all
concurrent steps, each agent's `apply_to_context()` unconditionally
overwrites `run_context.output_schema` with its own schema. This causes
agents to receive the wrong Pydantic schema, leading to
`ValidationError` or silently corrupt structured outputs.

The fix creates a shallow copy of `run_context` for each parallel step,
so `output_schema` is isolated per-step while `session_state` remains
shared (which is the intended behavior).

Closes #6590

parallel steps (the existing code already handles this). A shallow copy
creates a new `RunContext` instance with its own attribute slots, but
the `session_state` dict reference stays shared. Since `output_schema`
is replaced by reference assignment (not mutated in-place), shallow copy
is sufficient and cheaper than `deepcopy`.

tests:
- `test_each_parallel_step_gets_own_run_context` — verifies

subject: fix: knowledge_retriever ignored when search_knowledge=True (#6593)
message:
fix: knowledge_retriever ignored when search_knowledge=True (#6593)

## Summary

Fixes #6533 — `knowledge_retriever` is silently ignored when
`search_knowledge=True`.

### Root cause

In v2.3.x, knowledge tool registration used a single guard:

```python
if self.knowledge is not None or self.knowledge_retriever is not None:
```

This created one `search_knowledge_base` tool that routed through
`get_relevant_docs_from_knowledge()`, which checks `knowledge_retriever`
first and falls back to `knowledge.search()`.

In v2.4.0 (commit `a5e3928`), this was refactored into an `if/elif`:

```python
if resolved_knowledge is not None and agent.search_knowledge:
    knowledge_tools = resolved_knowledge.get_tools(...)  # bypasses retriever
elif agent.knowledge_retriever is not None and agent.search_knowledge:
    ...  # never reached when both are set
```

This caused two problems:
1. **Agent**: When both `knowledge` and `knowledge_retriever` are set,
`Knowledge.get_tools()` creates a tool that calls `self.search()`
directly, completely bypassing the custom retriever.
2. **Team**: Had no `elif` branch at all — custom retrievers were never
wired up.

### Fix

Restores the v2.3.x architecture for both Agent and Team:

- **Single `or` guard**: `if (knowledge is not None or
knowledge_retriever is not None) and search_knowledge`
- **One tool**: `create_knowledge_search_tool()` in `_default_tools.py`
creates a `search_knowledge_base` tool that routes through
`get_relevant_docs_from_knowledge()`
- **Routing**: `get_relevant_docs_from_knowledge()` checks
`knowledge_retriever` first, falls back to `knowledge.search()` — same
as v2.3.x
- **Agentic filters**: Supported via `enable_agentic_knowledge_filters`
flag, also routed through the same path

The user-facing API is unchanged: set `search_knowledge=True` and
optionally provide a `knowledge_retriever`. The framework routes to the
right implementation under the hood.

### Additional cleanup

- Removed dead tool factory functions that were no longer called after
the unified path was introduced
- Aligned Team filter validation with Agent behavior (`validate_filters`
parameter, only validated in agentic filters path)
- Added end-to-end tests that invoke the tool and verify the custom
retriever is actually called

| `agent/_tools.py` | Replace `if/elif` with single `or` guard, use

| `agent/_default_tools.py` | `create_knowledge_search_tool` with
agentic filter support |
| `team/_tools.py` | Same fix as agent — single `or` guard, wire up
